clue.text: Go too far starting heavy industry in plain

indicators.note: the selected letters sit inside the other word, which wraps around them

parts.note: plain, as in open and not hidden

indicators.note: what is starting a word is its opening letter, so only the fronts of the two words count

parts.note: the opening letters of heavy and industry

explanation.surface: Someone warns that starting heavy industry in open countryside goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhit a ball or a shot is to hit it beyond the target, overdoing things.

clue.text: Where you are, having conceded the first goal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the solver is reading the first down clue right now
second meaning: losing by a single score

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is self-referential: this very clue is numbered 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own grid position gives one sense; a team trailing by a single score after the opening goal gives the other.

clue.text: Almost merit promotion for reducing noise

definitions.note: a description of the object's use, standing for the noun

indicators.note: almost all of a word means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it
a plug is a piece of promotion or advertising

explanation.surface: Someone nearly deserves a promotion for keeping the office quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a job advance, but it means publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stopper pushed into the ear canal is used to block out sound and dampen loud surroundings.

clue.text: Lift engineer is hot!

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or rig it, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An admiring remark that the lift engineer is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun, a person, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up, often with ropes or a crane, is to lift it.

clue.text: Spell with natural sounding finish

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, like a school term

indicators.note: sounding means we hear the word rather than see it, so we write a word said the same way

parts.note: innate means inborn, natural

explanation.surface: A magic spell with a natural-sounding ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests magic or spelling, but it is a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or bring something to a close is to finish it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's cultural occupations

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: It evokes Lewis Carroll's Mad Hatter and his supposed cultural pastimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, music, theatre and literature are collectively known as this phrase, the creative pursuits of a culture.

clue.text: The grasses are oddly clipped

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in the odd positions, first, third and so on

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that the grasses have been cut unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suggests mowing, but it describes curt speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped speech is short and abrupt, which is what brief, curt replies are.

clue.text: Poet's near crazy for made-up language

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A poet is nearly mad about an invented language.
explanation.definitionFit: This international tongue was constructed by Zamenhof in 1887, so it is an invented, artificial means of communication.

clue.text: Regret taking on steady sales line

indicators.note: taking on something means taking it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to rue is to regret
even means steady, regular

explanation.surface: A firm regrets taking on a steady product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sales line' suggests a range of goods, but it is the line in the accounts showing income from sales.
explanation.definitionFit: In a company's accounts, income from sales appears as the top figure, often called turnover or income.

clue.text: The Blues Brothers send a solo piece back

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from right to left
a piece is only a part, so the letters are a section taken from inside the words

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, then the next two words, then the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: It evokes the Blues Brothers sending back a solo piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Blues Brothers' is a film title, but 'The Blues' is the definition and the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues means feeling melancholy, so the phrase is an informal name for unhappiness.

clue.text: Prior could be seen as more than a lord, perhaps

parts.note: an earl is one kind of lord, hence the 'perhaps'
the comparative ending, as in 'happier', meaning more so

explanation.surface: A religious prior might be seen as outranking a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monk, but it is the adjective meaning before. The joke reads the answer as 'more earl-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior and this word both describe something that happened before in time, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Enthused about old record being flagged again

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, wrapping the inner piece

parts.note: raved about something, praised it wildly
an EP, extended play, is an old vinyl record format

explanation.surface: Someone gushed about a vintage record that had been signalled again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flagged' suggests marked or tired, but here it means laid with flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are paving slabs, so a path flagged again has been given a fresh paved surface.

clue.text: It can provide or deny fuel

definitions.text: It can provide or deny fuel

parts.words: It can provide or deny fuel
parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about something that both supplies and withholds fuel
setter's reading: one sense is a lucky find of petroleum underground, the other a walkout by petroleum workers

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase has two senses: a discovery of a gusher, which gives fuel, and industrial action by refinery workers, which cuts supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a successful petroleum find and a stoppage by petroleum industry workers, giving or withholding supply.

clue.text: Explore scope for selection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to roam over an area
second meaning: the extent or span of something

explanation.walkthrough: The word also means a selection, as in a product line, so 'for selection' adds a third sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to wander widely; as a noun it means extent, reach, or an assortment of goods.

clue.text: His name means nothing, if he abandons good English

indicators.note: read backwards, the answer abandoning two letters leaves the word for nothing, so those letters sit inside it

parts.note: nil is zero, nothing
G for good and E for English

explanation.surface: A man's name is said to be worthless once he gives up good English.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs in reverse: take the G and E out of the answer and NIL is left, so the name means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a common English man's first name, which is what 'his name' points to.

clue.text: Opened in opposition to being excluded from work

indicators.note: being in opposition means taking the contrary of each word rather than the words themselves

parts.note: the opposite of opened
the opposite of in

explanation.surface: Striking workers opened a dispute with the bosses about being kept off the site.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'in opposition' does double duty: it is also the word whose opposite gives the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers shut out of their workplace by the employer during a dispute are barred from employment.

clue.text: Those missing beats seen to get in a tangle

indicators.note: things in a tangle are knotted and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Absent people are apparently seen beating themselves into a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are absent from work or school are those missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Lions come circulating; there's one!

indicators.note: circulating means moving around, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A safari spotter warns that lions are coming round and points one out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's one!' points at the punctuation mark in the clue itself, the one after 'circulating'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue itself contains this punctuation mark, so the exclamation literally points to an example in the text.

clue.text: Take on elite — it may make you look better!

definitions.text: it may make you look better!

parts.note: to face an opponent is to take them on
the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: A pep talk about confronting the best, which may improve your image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look better' suggests reputation, but it means appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic moisturiser applied to the skin is meant to improve your complexion and appearance.

clue.text: Gets emotional with pack over drink

parts.note: to pack a space is to fill it
to sup is to sip a drink

explanation.surface: Someone becomes tearful while packing up over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: When tears well up from strong feeling, a person becomes tearful or choked.

clue.text: Demolished luncheon dropping over the way to France

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
dropping something means letting it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone wolfed lunch before the trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, marked O on a scorecard. The answer is the nickname for the Channel Tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail tunnel under the English Channel links Britain with the French coast near Calais.

clue.text: Oscar role in picture that dazzles the eye

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a part played by an actor

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning role in a film that dazzles audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar and role suggest a film, but 'picture' is a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1960s movement painted geometric optical illusions designed to trick and dazzle the viewer's vision.

clue.text: Fashionable place in Texas journalist wrote up

parts.note: the Alamo is the historic mission in San Antonio

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist wrote up a trendy venue in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means in the current style, a borrowing for trendy or stylish.

clue.text: Some restaurants bar anyone so unconnected!

definitions.note: describes a person without a necktie
definitions.meaning: first meaning: without a necktie, against a dress code
second meaning: without ties or bonds

explanation.walkthrough: Smart restaurants may turn away a man without a necktie; read whimsically, the word also means having no ties at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking neckwear is the literal sense; lacking bonds or attachments is the punning sense of having no links.

clue.text: Bug where French enter London college

indicators.note: a word that enters another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the London School of Economics
the French word for where

explanation.surface: A virus or bug is found where French students enter a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parasitic insect counts as a bug in everyday speech, especially American usage for insects.

clue.text: Small gesture can warm things up

definitions.note: a description of what the appliance does, standing for its name

parts.note: micro means very small
a wave of the hand is a gesture

explanation.surface: A small friendly gesture can thaw relations between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm things up' suggests improving the mood, but it is the kitchen oven heating food.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen oven reheats leftovers quickly using electromagnetic radiation, so it heats food.

clue.text: Master in America means to take off …

definitions.note: the sign tells you to subtract

parts.note: M is short for Master, as in an MA
taken as written
the United States

explanation.surface: An American master craftsman explains how to remove something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic sign or word instructs you to subtract, which is to deduct or take away.

clue.text: … and start working group

parts.note: on means functioning, working
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: take off and start a working group.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, especially an illness or season, is its commencement.

clue.text: Local star is dejected, when the lights come on

parts.note: our own nearby star
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A local celebrity feels low when the stage lights come on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local star' suggests a hometown celebrity, but it is the star at the centre of our solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening dusk is the time of day when street lamps are switched on as it grows dark.

clue.text: Graceful line is what I'm all about

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
taken as written
'so me' is slang for typical of me

explanation.surface: A dancer boasts that a graceful line is exactly their style.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as L + IS + SO ME, using the slang 'that's so me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supple, slim and flexible body moves with grace, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Exercise taken by pupil at estate

indicators.note: the run of letters is held by the words that follow, sitting within them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A schoolchild on a housing estate takes some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: This system of controlled body-conditioning workouts, focusing on core strength, is a form of physical exercise.

clue.text: Nurse worried about limits of test for eccentrics

indicators.note: something worried about is shaken around, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of test

explanation.surface: A nurse frets over the outcome of a test given to odd patients.
explanation.walkthrough: A nutter is British slang for a crazy or eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for crazy or odd people, so it matches oddballs and cranks in a colloquial way.
